2610.08048.title: DAEDALUS: Bootstrapping Agent Memory from Self-Generated Tasks
2610.08048.paper_summary: LLM agents often lack the operational knowledge to act reliably in new environments, as they must discover specific tool behaviors or environment conventions on their own. Without memory of past attempts, they repeat the same mistakes across tasks, leading to more task failures and longer trajectories. To address this, agentic systems typically rely on human-written guidelines or on procedural memory built from training tasks and an oracle verifier, both of which require prior knowledge of the environment. We present DAEDALUS, a method for bootstrapping reusable agent memory from self-generated practice without existing tasks or oracle verifiers. DAEDALUS pairs two agents: an explorer that interacts with the environment to generate challenging yet solvable tasks, and a solver that attempts them. A heuristic is derived from each solver failure and accepted only after the solver repeatedly succeeds with that heuristic in context. These outcomes also provide feedback for the explorer to refine the difficulty of future tasks. Accepted heuristics are then consolidated into a memory bank for test-time use. Across AppWorld, $τ^2$-bench, and AutomationBench, DAEDALUS improves mean success rates by up to 15.9 points and pass^5 by up to 2.2x over a no-memory baseline, and is competitive with methods using training tasks, at a lower inference cost than most. We show that performance gains already emerge with a small exploration budget, and that its heuristics also benefit agents from other model families. Our ablations further reveal that solver traces provide the key information needed to derive effective heuristics, while factorizing early discoveries makes exploration more cost-efficient. Beyond memory construction, we find that the tasks generated by DAEDALUS can serve as a proxy for benchmark tasks when ranking models by performance. Code and artifacts: www.github.com/illuin-tech/daedalus.
2610.08048.paper_summary_zh: LLM 代理通常缺乏在新環境中可靠行動的操作知識，因為它們必須自行發現特定工具行為或環境規範。<lb/>如果沒有過去嘗試的記憶，它們會在任務中重複相同的錯誤，導致更多的任務失敗和更長的軌跡。<lb/>為了解決這個問題，代理系統通常依賴於人類撰寫的指南或從訓練任務和一個神諭驗證者構建的程序記憶，這兩者都需要對環境的先前知識。<lb/>我們提出了 DAEDALUS，一種從自生成的練習中啟動可重用代理記憶的方法，無需現有的任務或神諭驗證者。<lb/>DAEDALUS 配對了兩個代理：一個探索者與環境互動以生成具有挑戰性但可解決的任務，以及一個解決者嘗試這些任務。<lb/>每次解決者失敗後，將從中導出一個啟發式，並僅在解決者在該上下文中多次成功使用該啟發式後接受。<lb/>這些結果還為探索者提供反饋，以便細化未來任務的難度。<lb/>接受的啟發式隨後被整合到一個記憶庫中以供測試時使用。<lb/>在 AppWorld、$τ^2$-bench 和 AutomationBench 中，DAEDALUS 將平均成功率提高了最多 15.9 個點，pass^5 提高了最多 2.2 倍，相較於無記憶基線，其推理成本低於大多數使用訓練任務的方法。<lb/>我們展示了即使在小的探索預算下，性能增益已經出現，並且其啟發式也使來自其他模型系列的代理受益。<lb/>我們的消融實驗進一步揭示了解決者的追蹤提供了推導有效啟發式所需的關鍵信息，而將早期發現因素化使探索更具成本效益。<lb/>除了記憶構建之外，我們發現 DAEDALUS 生成的任務可以作為基準任務的代理，當按性能對模型進行排名時。<lb/>代碼和工件： www.github.com/illuin-tech/daedalus.
